answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation blog post dated 2026-07-01 (party statement, publisher NVIDIA), with quoted statements from Sharon AI CEO James Manning and Firmus co-CEO Tim Rosenfield, and item:e3/item:e4 drawn from the same post.
answer.note: Source claim: NVIDIA says a new business model lets AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers through a revenue-sharing and credit-support model, with NVIDIA earning standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity, which it describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. It also names Firmus's Batam, Indonesia DSX AI factory campus, expected to scale to 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs, and says AI cloud companies are already building DSX AI factories. What it supports: NVDA's own description of a channel in which it could earn product revenue and a usage-linked share of partner cloud revenue, and a stated forward supply plan (Firmus campus) that would require NVIDIA GPUs if built as described. Conditional interpretation: if the model operates as described, NVDA's revenue mix could shift toward recurring cloud-linked income on capacity financed or sold through AI cloud partners, and the Firmus plan is a supply lead for NVIDIA GPU demand over an unstated period. Limits on this reading: the source gives no revenue-share percentage, credit-support size, contract terms, signing status, or timing, so the magnitude of any earnings effect and the degree of NVDA's financial exposure through credit support are unknown. Counterexample check: every quoted fact could remain true while NVDA's economic gain is small or its credit exposure is large, or while the Firmus campus is delayed or uses GPUs bought through other channels, so the earnings-stream link stays a hypothesis until terms and filings are seen. Baseten, Fireworks AI and Together AI are cited as AI natives that use AI cloud capacity; they are not shown to buy from NVDA directly or to be parties to this model, so they inform end demand only. Sharon AI's statement is a collaboration quote with no quantities.
limitations: No revenue-share percentage, credit-support amount, guarantee cap, or contract term is disclosed for the new model, so NVDA's share of cloud revenue and its credit exposure cannot be sized.
The post does not state whether agreements with Sharon AI or Firmus are signed, binding or still under negotiation; signing status is unknown.
The Firmus figures of 360 MW and up to 170,000 GPUs are described as expected, with no completion date, phasing, financing or purchase schedule; they are a plan, not a confirmed order.
No NVDA financial figures tied to this model (revenue, deferred revenue, receivables, guarantees or commitments) are given in the source.
The source does not show that Baseten, Fireworks AI or Together AI buy from NVDA or are parties to the revenue-sharing model; their link to NVDA is inferred only as end demand.
The source is NVIDIA's own promotional statement with no independent verification of the model's adoption or economics.
follow_up: Search NVIDIA's next 10-Q and 10-K for disclosure of this revenue-sharing model, credit-support or guarantee arrangements, and related contingent liabilities, purchase commitments or receivables.
Check Sharon AI and Firmus announcements and filings for signed agreements, financing terms, and dated deployment milestones for the Batam campus and other DSX AI factories.
Verify whether the Firmus 360 MW / 170,000 GPU figures appear in Firmus or Indonesian project records with a stated timeline and funding source.
Look for any disclosed NVDA revenue-share or usage-linked income line in later quarterly results and track whether it is reported separately from product revenue.
